newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria reports increase in banking fraud.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria reports increase in banking fraud.

text.p: Cases of fraud in the Nigerian banking system rose by 151 percent to 606 in 1996 from 241 in 1995, the regulatory body, Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), said in its annual report published on Wednesday.
The amount of money involved also rose within the period to 1.6 billion naira from 1.01 billion naira.

"If the increasing wave of malpractices in the banking industry is not checked, it will pose additional threat to the stability and performance of the industry as a whole," said NDIC chief executive John Ebhodaghe, who presented the report to journalists.
He said equally worrying was an emerging trend whereby an increasing number of senior management staff of banks were involved in malpractices while the figure for lower ranked staff was declining.
A total of 218 managers, officers and accountants were involved in fraud during the period under review as against 151 in 1995, while the figure for other staff fell to 156 from 245.
Ebhodaghe said further analysis of the figures showed that 10 banks, which comprise less than 10 percent of banking sector, were responsible for 65.76 percent of the reported cases.
The most common malpractices were presenting forged cheques, granting unauthorised overdrafts, posting fictitious credits as well as fraudulent transfers and withdrawals.
In a bid to restore sanity to the banking sector, so-called failed banks tribunals have since 1995 jailed scores of bankers and others found to have looted banks through unsecured loans.

Some of the banks that fell into distress because of such fraud were taken over by the central bank and offered for sale to investors willing to recapitalise them but this has so far not yielded any results.
According to the regulatory authorities 48 or 42 percent of the country's 115 commercial and merchant banks are in distress.
